claims.metric: predictive log-likelihood and RMSE improvement over state-of-the-art
claims.quote: We show a considerable improvement in predictive log-likelihood and RMSE compared to existing state-of-the-art methods

claims.metric: RMSE and uncertainty estimation improvement over VI and PBP
claims.quote: In the results section we compare dropout to these approaches and show a significant improvement in both RMSE and uncertainty estimation.

claims.metric: predictive log-likelihood and RMSE improvement over state-of-the-art
claims.quote: We then show that using dropout's uncertainty we can obtain a considerable improvement in predictive log-likelihood and RMSE compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

claims.metric: quantitative assessment in reinforcement learning
claims.quote: We give a quantitative assessment of the model's performance in the setting of reinforcement learning on a task similar to that used in deep reinforcement learning (Mnih et al., 2015).

claims.metric: 4-layer models convergence
claims.quote: Not plotted are the models with 4 layers as these converge to the same results.

claims.metric: periodicity capture failure

conditions.comparison: GP with suitable covariance would capture

claims.quote: Extrapolating the observed data, none of the models can capture the periodicity (although with a suitable covariance function the GP will capture it well).

claims.metric: GP predictive uncertainty increase at x*
claims.quote: The GP model represents this by increasing its predictive uncertainty – in effect declaring that the predictive value might be 0 but the model is uncertain.

claims.metric: MC dropout captures uncertainty increase at x*
claims.quote: This behaviour is captured in MC dropout as well.

claims.metric: incorrect predictive mean but increased std dev expresses uncertainty
claims.quote: Even though the models in figures 2 have an incorrect predictive mean, the increased standard deviation expresses the models' uncertainty about the point.

claims.metric: uncertainty trend far from data: ReLU increases, TanH stays bounded
claims.quote: Note that the uncertainty is increasing far from the data for the ReLU model, whereas for the TanH model it stays bounded.

claims.metric: TanH uncertainty convergence across dropout probabilities
claims.quote: Models initialised with dropout probability 0.1 initially exhibit smaller uncertainty than the ones initialised with dropout probability 0.2, but towards the end of the optimisation when the model has converged the uncertainty is almost indistinguishable.

claims.metric: dropout model moments converge to approximated GP moments

conditions.target: approximated GP model mean and uncertainty

claims.quote: It seems that the moments of the dropout models converge to the moments of the approximated GP model – its mean and uncertainty.

claims.metric: failed to fit data with fewer layers
claims.quote: It is worth mentioning that we attempted to fit the data with models with a smaller number of layers unsuccessfully.

claims.metric: predicted classes for 12 rotated images
claims.quote: For the 12 images, the model predicts classes [1 1 1 1 1 5 5 7 7 7 7 7].

claims.metric: rotated digit 1 classified as 5 for images 6-7 with extremely large uncertainty
claims.quote: A scatter of 100 forward passes of the softmax input and output for dropout LeNet. On the X axis is a rotated image of the digit 1. The input is classiﬁed as digit 5 for images 6-7, even though model uncertainty is extremly large (best viewed in colour).

claims.metric: Dropout outperforms VI and PBP on RMSE and test log-likelihood except Yacht RMSE

conditions.exception: Yacht Hydrodynamics where PBP obtains better RMSE

claims.quote: Dropout signiﬁcantly outperforms all other models both in terms of RMSE as well as test log-likelihood on all datasets apart from Yacht, for which PBP obtains better RMSE.

claims.metric: Boston Housing median RMSE and predictive log-likelihood with IQR
claims.quote: For example, on the Boston Housing dataset dropout achieves median RMSE of 2.68 with an IQR interval of [2.45, 3.35] and predictive log-likelihood median of -2.34 with IQR [-2.54, -2.29].

claims.metric: Concrete Strength median RMSE
claims.quote: In the Concrete Strength dataset dropout achieves median RMSE of 5.15.

claims.metric: model running time comparable to PBP Theano

conditions.comparison: dropout model (with BO) vs PBP Theano

claims.quote: However our model's running time (including BO) is comparable to PBP's Theano implementation.

claims.metric: Naval Propulsion time per split

conditions.measurement: average per split (start-to-finish, divided by number of splits)

claims.quote: On Naval Propulsion for example our model takes 276 seconds on average per split (start-to-finish, divided by the number of splits).

claims.metric: model training time vs PBP
claims.quote: With the optimal parameters BO found, model training took 95 seconds. This is in comparison to PBP's 220 seconds.

claims.metric: Kin8nm training time with and without BO vs PBP
claims.quote: For Kin8nm our model requires 188 seconds on average including BO, 65 seconds without, compared to PBP's 156 seconds.

claims.metric: MC dropout improves over standard dropout weight averaging and near-zero dropout

conditions.comparison: MC dropout vs standard dropout weight averaging vs dropout prob near zero

claims.quote: We observed an improvement using this estimate compared to the standard dropout weight averaging, and also compared to much smaller dropout probabilities (near zero).

claims.metric: dropout significantly affects LL and RMSE even at small probability
claims.quote: This demonstrates that dropout significantly affects the predictive log-likelihood and RMSE, even though the dropout probability is fairly small.
